:::{#thm-poisson-rate-ratio}
#### Rate ratios in Poisson regression

In a [Poisson regression model](poisson-regression.qmd#def-poisson-regression),
suppose [covariate](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate) $x_j$ enters the [linear function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-linear-function) $\lnf{\lambda(\vx)}$
only through the single [term](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-term) $\b_j x_j$
(no interactions or transformations involving $x_j$).
Let $\vx$ and $\vxs$ be two [covariate patterns](logistic-inference.qmd#def-covariate-pattern)
that are identical except that $x_j = a$ and $x^*_j = b$.
Then

$$\rateratio(\vx : \vxs) = \expf{\b_j (a - b)}$$ {#eq-poisson-rate-ratio}

and for any common [exposure magnitude](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-exposure) $t > 0$,
the [ratio](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-ratio) of [expected counts](basic-statistical-methods.qmd#def-expected-count) is the same [rate ratio](poisson-regression.qmd#def-rate-ratio):

$$\frac{\mu(\vx, t)}{\mu(\vxs, t)} = \rateratio(\vx : \vxs)$$

:::

::: proof
Because $\vx$ and $\vxs$ agree on every [covariate](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate) except $x_j$,
every [term](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-term) of $\lnf{\lambda(\vx)}$ except $\b_j x_j$ is shared with $\lnf{\lambda(\vxs)}$:

$$
\ba
\lnf{\lambda(\vx)} - \lnf{\lambda(\vxs)}
&= \paren{\b_0 + \b_1 x_1 + \lds + \red{\b_j a} + \lds + \b_p x_p} \\
&\phantom{={}} - \paren{\b_0 + \b_1 x_1 + \lds + \red{\b_j b} + \lds + \b_p x_p}
&& \text{(substitute the linear function)} \\
&= \red{\b_j a} - \red{\b_j b}
&& \text{(cancel the shared terms)} \\
&= \red{\b_j (a - b)}
&& \text{(factor out } \b_j \text{)}
\ea
$$

Then the [rate ratio](poisson-regression.qmd#def-rate-ratio) is:

$$
\ba
\rateratio(\vx : \vxs)
&= \frac{\lambda(\vx)}{\lambda(\vxs)}
&& \text{(definition of rate ratio)} \\
&= \frac{\expf{\lnf{\lambda(\vx)}}}{\expf{\lnf{\lambda(\vxs)}}}
&& \text{(exponential undoes the log)} \\
&= \expf{\lnf{\lambda(\vx)} - \lnf{\lambda(\vxs)}}
&& \text{(quotient rule for exponentials)} \\
&= \expf{\b_j (a - b)}
&& \text{(substitute the difference of linear functions)}
\ea
$$

For the [expected counts](basic-statistical-methods.qmd#def-expected-count) at a common exposure $t > 0$:

$$
\ba
\frac{\mu(\vx, t)}{\mu(\vxs, t)}
&= \frac{\lambda(\vx) \cdot t}{\lambda(\vxs) \cdot t}
&& \text{(Poisson regression mean function)} \\
&= \frac{\lambda(\vx)}{\lambda(\vxs)}
&& \text{(cancel } t > 0 \text{)} \\
&= \rateratio(\vx : \vxs)
&& \text{(definition of rate ratio)}
\ea
$$

:::
